_description: The orbit model's physical referee (plan 28 §D, doc 111 §1.48): Gliese 710's closest approach to the Sun, the best-known future stellar encounter. The Gaia DR3 row is the archive's (gaiadr3.gaia_source, source_id 4270814637616488064, fetched 2026-11-17 by the recorded query); the published approaches are full-potential integrations on earlier releases. The model's own value (the second-order epicycle about the star's and the Sun's guiding centres in the cited local potential, ONE home packages/physics/src/sky/galactic-orbits.cjs) is pinned as a REGRESSION value; the published pair brackets it and is the physical check. Gate: tools/verify/star-catalogue.js. A hand-written record: no generator.

gaiaDr3.query: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_error, pmra, pmdec, radial_velocity, radial_velocity_error, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE source_id = 4270814637616488064

published.source: Bailer-Jones, Rybizki, Andrae & Fouesneau 2018, A&A 616, A37 (Gaia DR2)
de la Fuente Marcos & de la Fuente Marcos 2022 (Gaia EDR3, as cited for the encounter)

model.evaluator: the second-order epicycle (galactic-orbits.cjs orbitElements / galactocentricPositionAt), the Sun on its own, from epoch J2016.0

straightLine.note: the same astrometry on a straight line — the tidal field moves the approach by 0.004 pc over 1.3 Myr
